nodes.title: Power Apps: canvas, model-driven, and PCF: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Power Apps is the app layer of the Power Platform. PL-400 expects you to know when to use a canvas app vs a model-driven app, and how to extend either with code components (PCF).

flashcards.back: Canvas apps give pixel-level control over the UI and can connect to many data sources — best for task-focused, tailored experiences. Model-driven apps are generated from the Dataverse data model and security — best for complex, data-centric line-of-business apps where consistency matters more than custom layout.

flashcards.front: What is the Power Apps Component Framework (PCF)?
flashcards.back: PCF lets you build reusable code components (controls) in TypeScript/HTML that plug into canvas and model-driven apps, replacing or augmenting standard fields and grids. Use it when no out-of-the-box control meets the UX requirement.

flashcards.front: How do canvas apps talk to data?
flashcards.back: Through connectors. Dataverse is the native, most capable connector; others reach SQL, SharePoint, or any REST API via custom connectors. Delegation matters: push filtering/sorting to the source so you don't hit the local record cap on large datasets.

A wrapper around a REST API (described by an OpenAPI/Swagger definition) that makes its operations available to Power Apps and Power Automate. It handles auth (API key, OAuth2) and surfaces actions as first-class steps — the standard way to integrate an external system.

questions.q: A business analyst is asked to explain the four core low-code product families that make up Microsoft Power Platform. Which list correctly names all four?
choices: Power BI, Power Apps, Power Query, Power Pivot
Power BI, Power Apps, Dynamics 365, Microsoft Fabric
Power BI, Power Apps, Power Automate, Azure Logic Apps
Power BI, Power Apps, Power Automate, Power Pages
questions.explanation: Microsoft Power Platform consists of four core products: Power BI (analytics), Power Apps (low-code apps), Power Automate (workflow automation) and Power Pages (low-code external websites). Copilot Studio is often listed alongside them as an additional family. Power Query and Power Pivot are Excel/Power BI features, Dynamics 365 and Microsoft Fabric are separate product lines, and Azure Logic Apps is a pro-developer integration service in Azure — none of these are Power Platform pillars themselves.

questions.q: A sales operations team needs to digitise a Dynamics 365 Sales record-management process with consistent forms, views, dashboards and business process flows tightly coupled to Dataverse tables. Which type of Power Apps application best fits this requirement?
choices: A model-driven app built on top of Dataverse
A canvas app pointing to a SharePoint list
A Power Pages site for external customers
A Power BI paginated report
questions.explanation: Model-driven apps are generated from a Dataverse data model and automatically render forms, views, dashboards and business process flows that match the underlying tables — exactly the design goal here, and the same technology Dynamics 365 first-party apps are built on. Canvas apps start from a blank screen and are best for pixel-perfect, task-focused UIs over many data sources but are not generated from the data model. Power Pages produces external-facing websites, and Power BI paginated reports are read-only reporting artefacts — neither manages records.

questions.q: An IT team wants a Power Automate flow to run every weekday at 06:00 to refresh an inventory report, with no trigger from a user or another system. Which type of flow is purpose-built for this?
choices: An automated cloud flow
A scheduled cloud flow
An instant cloud flow
A desktop flow (Power Automate for desktop)
questions.explanation: A scheduled cloud flow runs on a recurrence (for example, every weekday at 06:00) without any external trigger, which matches the requirement exactly. Automated cloud flows are triggered by an event in a connector (a new email, a row added, etc.); instant cloud flows are triggered manually by a user from a button, mobile app or Teams; and desktop flows automate UI interactions on a Windows desktop using Power Automate for desktop (RPA) and are themselves invoked by other flows or by a user.

questions.q: A finance director wants self-service dashboards that connect to multiple data sources, transform the data, build a semantic model and let executives drill through interactive visuals on the web and on mobile. Which Power Platform service is purpose-built for this?
choices: Power Apps (canvas apps)
Power Automate (cloud flows)
Power BI (Desktop, Service and Mobile)
Power Pages (external websites)
questions.explanation: Power BI is the analytics service of Power Platform: Power BI Desktop authors models, the Power BI Service publishes dashboards and reports, and the Power BI Mobile apps deliver interactive visuals on phones and tablets. Power Apps builds transactional apps, Power Automate orchestrates workflows and Power Pages hosts low-code external websites — none of them is an analytics and dashboarding product.

nodes.title: Microsoft Dataverse: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Dataverse is the data platform underneath the Power Platform — a managed, relational store with built-in security, business logic, and a uniform Web API. PL-400 leans on it heavily: most Power Apps, plug-ins, and automations read and write Dataverse.

flashcards.front: What is a Dataverse table (formerly entity)?
flashcards.back: A table is a typed set of rows with columns, relationships, keys, and its own security. Standard tables (Account, Contact) ship with the platform; custom tables are added per solution. Each table exposes an OData/Web API endpoint automatically.

flashcards.front: How do you query Dataverse from code?
flashcards.back: Use the Web API — an OData v4 REST endpoint at /api/data/v9.x. GET with $select/$filter/$expand for reads, POST/PATCH/DELETE for writes. The SDK (IOrganizationService) wraps the same operations for plug-ins and server-side code.

flashcards.front: How is access controlled in Dataverse?
flashcards.back: Security roles grant privileges (create/read/write/delete/append) at access levels (user, business unit, parent-child, organization). Rows are owned by a user or team; business units scope visibility. This is row- and column-level security, not just table-level.

flashcards.front: Business rules vs plug-ins for logic?
flashcards.back: Business rules are no-code, run on the form and server for simple validation/defaults. Plug-ins are .NET code on the event pipeline for complex or cross-table logic. Prefer the lightest tool that meets the requirement — business rules first, plug-ins when you need real code.

questions.q: A service desk lead wants to build a conversational AI agent that answers common IT questions, triggers a Power Automate flow to reset a password and can be deployed to Microsoft Teams and a public website with no traditional coding. Which Power Platform product is designed for this?
choices: Power BI Q&A
AI Builder forms processing
Power Apps portals
Microsoft Copilot Studio
questions.explanation: Microsoft Copilot Studio (the rebranded Power Virtual Agents) is the low-code product for designing conversational agents (topics, generative answers, multi-channel publishing) and calling Power Automate flows for back-end actions such as password resets. Power BI Q&A returns natural-language answers about a dataset, not a conversational agent; AI Builder forms processing extracts fields from documents; and Power Apps portals is the old name for Power Pages, which builds external websites rather than chatbots.

questions.q: A maker joining a Power Platform project keeps hearing that Dataverse is where the app's data should live, and wants a clear description of what Dataverse actually is. Which statement best describes Microsoft Dataverse in the context of Power Platform?
choices: A secure, scalable data platform with standard and custom tables, business logic and role-based security that is the default data store for model-driven Power Apps
A cloud file-share service used to store the Excel and CSV files that canvas Power Apps read from
A self-service ETL tool that moves data from on-premises systems into Power BI semantic models
A relational database engine that runs only on Azure SQL Managed Instance
questions.explanation: Microsoft Dataverse is the managed data platform behind Power Platform. It provides standard and custom tables, relationships, business rules, calculated and rollup columns, role-based security and is the default data store for model-driven apps and Dynamics 365 first-party apps. It is not a file-share (that role is filled by OneDrive/SharePoint), it is not an ETL tool (Power Query and Dataflows handle ingestion), and it is implemented on Azure services but is not the same product as Azure SQL Managed Instance.

questions.q: A maker wants to connect a canvas Power App to Salesforce and to an on-premises SQL Server database. Both connectors are categorised as premium. What does this mean for licensing?
choices: Premium connectors are free for any Microsoft 365 user as long as the app is published in a managed environment
Each user who runs the app needs a Power Apps premium licence (per app or per user); the standard Microsoft 365 plan alone is not sufficient
Premium connectors can only be called from Power Automate flows and never from Power Apps canvas apps
Premium connectors are technically identical to standard connectors and require no additional licensing beyond Microsoft 365
questions.explanation: Power Platform connectors are divided into standard and premium tiers. Standard connectors (SharePoint, Outlook, OneDrive for Business, Teams, etc.) are usable with a Microsoft 365 licence that includes Power Apps/Power Automate seeded use rights, but premium connectors (Salesforce, on-premises SQL Server via the gateway, Oracle, HTTP, custom connectors, etc.) require a Power Apps premium licence (per app or per user) or an equivalent Power Automate premium licence for every user who runs the app. Premium is not free, and premium connectors work in both Power Apps and Power Automate.

questions.q: A back-office team wants Power Automate to automatically read scanned vendor invoices (PDF and image), extract the vendor name, invoice number, total amount and line items, and write the results to Dataverse — with no custom ML training to start with. Which Power Platform capability is purpose-built for this?
choices: Power BI key influencers visual
Power Apps formula bar with Power Fx
AI Builder invoice processing (prebuilt model)
Microsoft Dataverse business rules
questions.explanation: AI Builder is the AI capability of Power Platform and ships prebuilt models such as invoice processing, receipt processing, business card reader and ID reader that can be called directly from Power Apps and Power Automate with no training required. The Power BI key influencers visual explains drivers of a metric in a report, the Power Fx formula bar evaluates expressions in canvas apps and Dataverse business rules enforce field-level validation — none of them perform document AI.

nodes.title: Power Platform solutions and ALM: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Solutions are how you package, version, and move Power Platform components (tables, apps, flows, plug-ins) between environments. Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) on PL-400 is about doing that reliably from dev to test to production.

flashcards.back: Unmanaged is the editable, source form you build in your dev environment — components can be changed and the solution itself isn't a deployment boundary. Managed is the locked, deployable artifact you import into test/production; it can be cleanly upgraded or uninstalled. Develop unmanaged, ship managed.

Separate dev, test, and production environments isolate change: you build in dev, validate in test, and release to production by importing the managed solution. Never edit components directly in production — it breaks the ALM chain and can't be cleanly upgraded.

flashcards.front: How do you automate solution deployment?
flashcards.back: Use the Power Platform Build Tools (or Power Platform CLI 'pac') in a pipeline to export the unmanaged solution from dev, build a managed version, and import it to the next environment. Pipelines in Power Platform also provide a managed, low-code path for the same export/import flow.

flashcards.front: What are environment variables and connection references for?
flashcards.back: They externalise per-environment values (URLs, IDs) and connections so the same managed solution works in dev, test, and prod without hard-coded settings. You set their values at or after import — a key practice for clean, repeatable deployments.

questions.q: A marketing team needs to publish an external-facing, low-code website where customers can sign in, browse products and submit support cases that are stored in Microsoft Dataverse. Which Power Platform product is purpose-built for this scenario?
choices: Power Apps model-driven app published anonymously
Power BI public publish-to-web report
SharePoint Online communication site with a Dataverse connector
Power Pages site backed by Dataverse
questions.explanation: Power Pages (the successor to Power Apps portals) is the low-code product for building external-facing websites, with anonymous and authenticated access, page templates, forms and lists, all natively bound to Microsoft Dataverse — exactly the scenario described. Model-driven apps are intended for internal authenticated business users and cannot be published anonymously, Power BI publish-to-web exposes a read-only report (and is unsuitable for sensitive data), and a SharePoint communication site is not the Power Platform product designed for external Dataverse-bound web experiences.

questions.q: A Power Platform administrator wants to isolate work-in-progress canvas apps and flows from production apps and from customer-facing apps, with separate Dataverse databases and separate data loss prevention (DLP) policies for each. Which Power Platform construct provides this isolation boundary?
choices: Environments
Solutions
Connection references
Dataverse business units
questions.explanation: An environment is the container in Power Platform that holds apps, flows, connections and (optionally) a Dataverse database, and it is the primary boundary for security, geographic data residency and DLP policy enforcement. Typical patterns use separate Development, Test and Production environments. Solutions are ALM packages that group customisations and move them between environments. Connection references abstract a specific connection so it can be retargeted across environments. Business units are an internal hierarchy inside a single Dataverse database for record ownership and do not create environment-level isolation.

questions.q: A maker familiar with Excel formulas asks which low-code expression language is used to write logic in the Power Apps canvas formula bar (and increasingly in other Power Platform tools).
choices: DAX (Data Analysis Expressions)
Power Fx
Power Query M
Office Scripts (TypeScript)
questions.explanation: Power Fx is the open-source, Excel-like low-code language used in the Power Apps canvas formula bar and is being extended to other Power Platform tools (Dataverse formula columns, Copilot Studio, etc.). DAX is the formula language of Power BI semantic models and Analysis Services; Power Query M is the data-transformation language used in Power Query and dataflows; and Office Scripts is a TypeScript-based automation language for Excel on the web — none of them is the canvas-app formula language.

questions.q: A development team builds canvas apps, model-driven apps, flows and Dataverse tables in a Development environment and needs to move all of those customisations together into a Test environment in a controlled, repeatable way. Which Power Platform feature is designed for this application lifecycle management (ALM) workflow?
choices: Manually rebuilding each component in the Test environment
Exporting each app and flow individually as a ZIP file and importing it
Packaging the components into a managed solution and importing the solution into the Test environment
Sharing each component directly with users in the Test environment from the maker portal
questions.explanation: Solutions are the unit of ALM in Power Platform: they collect Dataverse tables, canvas and model-driven apps, flows, connection references, environment variables and other components, and can be exported as managed solutions for promotion to downstream environments (Test, Production) in a controlled, repeatable way that supports source control and pipelines. Manual rebuilds and one-off exports of individual artefacts are error-prone and not repeatable, and sharing components with users does not move them between environments at all.
